entries.title: Hillside Snowfall and Layered Accumulation
entries.description: A sloped terrain mesh receives falling snow particles that stick, slide, or bounce depending on impact speed, gradually building a white layer with thickness visualized by color bands and numeric labels at sample points.
entries.seed: Hillside Snowfall and Layered Accumulation: A sloped terrain mesh receives falling snow particles that stick, slide, or bounce depending on impact speed, gradually building a white layer with thickness visualized by color bands and numeric labels at sample points.

entries.title: Roof Load and Snow Shedding
entries.description: A simple house with pitched roofs accumulates snow spheres that compress into a packed layer, while portions periodically slide off the roof edges as slabs, colliding with the ground and updating a live “roof load” meter.
entries.seed: Roof Load and Snow Shedding: A simple house with pitched roofs accumulates snow spheres that compress into a packed layer, while portions periodically slide off the roof edges as slabs, colliding with the ground and updating a live “roof load” meter.

entries.title: Car Driving Through Fresh Snow
entries.description: A box-shaped car drives along a flat plane where snowflakes accumulate, compress under the tires, and leave sunken tracks, with snow particles kicked sideways as small sprays that settle into ridges.
entries.seed: Car Driving Through Fresh Snow: A box-shaped car drives along a flat plane where snowflakes accumulate, compress under the tires, and leave sunken tracks, with snow particles kicked sideways as small sprays that settle into ridges.

entries.title: Wind-Driven Snow Dunes and Drifts
entries.description: A flat field with fence posts experiences lateral wind that pushes falling snow particles across the surface, causing snow to pile up on the leeward side of obstacles, forming drifts that grow, shift, and reshape over time.

entries.title: Avalanche Formation on a Mountain Slope
entries.description: Snow layers accumulate on a steep mountain, each layer shown in a different semi-transparent color; when a threshold is reached, the upper layers detach and slide down as a flowing particle cloud, scouring and re-depositing snow.

entries.title: Icicle Growth from Melting and Refreezing Snow
entries.description: A roof edge has a snow layer that slowly melts into droplets, which fall, collide with an icicle tip, and refreeze, causing translucent icicles to grow downward while a temperature slider controls melt/refreeze rates.

entries.title: Snow Accumulation on Tree Branches
entries.description: A branching tree structure collects falling snow that sticks to upper surfaces, piling into rounded caps; shaking the tree trunk triggers vibrations that detach some snow, which falls, breaks apart, and redistributes on the ground.

entries.title: Urban Street Snow Plowing
entries.description: Buildings line a street where snow constantly falls and accumulates on road and sidewalks; a moving plow box pushes and piles snow into compacted banks along the curb, with snow particles bouncing off walls and streetlights.
